newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower on dollar short-covering.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower on dollar short-covering.

text.p: Dollar short-covering in line with strengthening U.S. unit against the yen on the world market pushed the won to a lower close on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said dollar buying interest became active from the afternoon session as the dollar/yen soared to 117.75.
A widened trade deficit in September also boosted dollar buying interest. The customs-cleared trade shortfall expanded to $1.54 billion from $643 million a year earlier.
The won closed at 821.00 after opening at 820.70. It moved in a 821.80-820.20 range.
The market will be closed on Thursday for a national day.
Friday's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 820.90 against 821.80 today.
"Given importer deals due, we are planning to cover the current dollar short-position and then go long," said a Commerical Bank of Korea dealer.

Dealers said anticipation of an inflow of foreign funds destined for the Seoul bourse caused the dollar selling in the morning session. But lukewarm interests by foreign investors on the stock market bucked the early trend in the afternoon.
Dealers forecast the dolalr would move in a 819.50-822.00 won range on Friday. -- YEOM YOON-JEONG (822) 727 5647
